items.title: Hunter Biden Launches LAPTOP Meme Coin
points: Drops Sept. 9 on Base (an Ethereum-linked blockchain network); named after Hunter Biden's laptop whose contents leaked weeks before the 2020 election.
20% of token supply airdropped to holders of TRUMP coin who lost money, plus subscribers of the LAPTOP Substack and Andrew Callaghan's Channel 5.

Founders, including Hunter Biden, retain 30% on a 2-year vesting schedule (tokens unlock gradually over time); another 30% burns (permanently destroyed) on milestones like a Bitcoin all-time high or a Democratic 2028 presidential win.
Remaining 20% funds charity donations, liquidity provision (funds that keep a market tradeable), exchange fees, and legal/accounting costs.

items.title: Bitcoin Price Action & Market Structure
points: Bitcoin opened the week at $78,829, was rejected from $82K twice in the past two weeks, and trades near $79,011, down 0.8% in 24 hours.
84% of traders are betting on a rally to $84K (needing only a 6.6% gain) versus 16% betting on a drop to $55K (a steeper 30% decline).
Analysts are split between a trend reversal higher and a 'Bart Simpson pattern' (a chart shape resembling Bart's head, marking a sharp pump followed by a sudden crash) that could send price to $65K.
The market holds $235K in trader positions expiring in seven months, pointing to notable leverage (borrowed money used to amplify trading bets) heading into that date.

items.title: Chainlink Oracle Integration Boost
points: Chainlink hit an 8-month high after Bottomline, a top-3 SWIFT (the global bank messaging network used for interbank payments) services provider handling $16 trillion annually, integrated Chainlink's oracle network (software that feeds real-world data to blockchains).
The integration is seen as major validation from traditional finance for decentralized data infrastructure.

items.title: $320M Bitcoin Withdrawn from Liquid by Alleged White-Hat Hackers
points: Alleged white-hat hackers (security researchers who exploit vulnerabilities to expose or fix them, not to steal) withdrew $320M in Bitcoin from Liquid, Blockstream's sidechain (a separate blockchain linked to Bitcoin for added features).
The hackers are communicating via PGP-signed messages (cryptographically verified notes proving authorship) embedded directly in blockchain transactions.

items.title: Dormant Bitcoin Wallets Reawaken
points: An ancient Bitcoin wallet that turned an original $120 investment into $3M has become active again.
It joins at least three other long-dormant wallets that have recently sprung back to life, part of a growing trend.
Separately, a hacker linked to the Coldcard hardware wallet breach moved $7.7M from a stolen Bitcoin haul.
